column1: # Mutation-testing baselines — a RATCHET, not a to-do list, and NOT a claim that the
# remaining survivors are harmless.
# SPANS IS AT ITS FLOOR — 10, and all ten are EQUIVALENT MUTANTS (measured 2026-08-13).
# Do not spend another pass on `spans`. Tests were written for all ten, the file was
# registered in MODULE_TESTS[spans], coverage reached 98%, and the count did not move —
# because none of the ten can change observable behaviour:
#   * a corrupted `style` default or fallback is normalised back, and `_placeholder`
#     falls through to the label form for ANY unrecognised value (incl. None);
#   * `not text or not spans` -> `and` reaches the same answer via `if not applied`;
#   * `char_start > cursor` -> `>=` and `cursor < n` -> `<=` append the empty string;
#   * both `build_word_offsets` mutants sit on the FIRST `idx < 0` guard, where the
#     fallback `text.find(token)` re-finds the same index.
# Full reasoning: backend/tests/redaction/test_apply_redactions_mutants.py.
# Lowering this baseline requires changing spans.py, not adding tests.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
# "Kill every surviving mutant" is not a finishable goal on this codebase: an AST census of
# lockout's 149 survivors (regenerate mutmut's mutants from the source, map each survivor back
# to the line it edits, ask whether that line is inside a logging call) finds 58 that edit a log
# string and 8 that flip a condition guarding only a log call. No caller can observe those, and
# asserting on log text creates tests that break on every reword. Without a bounded definition
# of done, each pass closes a few real gaps and leaves a large residue — which reads as no
# progress.
# So the gate is: the survivor count for a module may go DOWN, never UP. A new untested
# predicate raises it and fails `--check-baseline`. That is the same shape as the coverage
# `fail_under` ratchet in backend/pyproject.toml, and for the same reason.
# READ THE NUMBERS AS A CEILING, NOT AS AN ALL-CLEAR. The same census over all six modules puts
# 167 of the 636 survivors (26%) in the log-string / log-branch bucket. The other 461 are
# ordinary predicates, comparisons, assignments and default arguments — code a caller CAN
# observe, and each one is a line the suite executes without checking. The counts below bound
# the residue; they do not excuse it.
# This file is READ by `./scripts/run-mutation-tests.sh --check-baseline`. It is not
# documentation: a checked-in table nothing reads goes stale, which is exactly how
# `expected-schemas.tsv` died. It went stale here anyway — two of the notes below described
# measurements nobody had made (see spans and lockout) — so every note now states what was
# measured and how.
# ⚠️ ALL SIX ROWS WERE RE-MEASURED FROM SCRATCH 2026-08-28 (spans, lockout, security, session,
# dependencies, password_policy — see each row). `--check-baseline` now passes for all six.
# ⚠️ 2026-10-30: auth/lockout.py was split into lockout.py + lockout_store.py + lockout_admin.py
# (keys `lockout`, `lockout_store`, `lockout_admin`). NOT re-measured yet. 2026-11-12: all three keys now
# have a DERIVED row (38 / 16 / 6 of the last pre-split log, by function); the run replaces them.
# ⚠️ 2026-11-01: api/endpoints/auth/dependencies.py was split into dependencies.py +
# lifecycle_gates.py + external_token.py (keys `dependencies`, `lifecycle_gates`, `external_token`).
# NOT re-measured yet. 2026-11-12: all three keys now have a DERIVED row (30 / 38 / 11 of the 79 survivors of
# the last whole-module run, .mutation/dependencies.log, cb357005f, by function); the run replaces them.
# HOW TO UPDATE
#   ./scripts/run-mutation-tests.sh --clean            # stale cached verdicts are the #1 trap
#   ./scripts/run-mutation-tests.sh --module <name>
#   ./scripts/run-mutation-tests.sh --check-baseline <name>
# Lower the number when you have added tests. NEVER raise it to make a run pass — that is the
# one move this file exists to prevent. Raising it needs a reason in the commit message.
# COVERAGE is recorded alongside because a survivor count is meaningless without it: a module
# whose selected tests execute 56% of it reports survivors that measure test SELECTION, not
# test strength. That happened to `lockout` and produced 41 false findings in `dependencies`.
# module<TAB>max_survivors<TAB>min_coverage_pct<TAB>measured_on<TAB>note

The 10 old ones: a corrupted `style` default or fallback is normalised back and `_placeholder` falls through to the label form for ANY unrecognised value; `not text or not spans`->`and` reaches the same answer via `if not applied`; `char_start > cursor`->`>=` and `cursor < n`->`<=` append the empty string; both `build_word_offsets` mutants sit on the FIRST `idx < 0` guard where the fallback `text.find(token)` re-finds the same index. column5: 17 of 243 mutants survive and ALL ARE EQUIVALENT (all-module run 2026-11-13, tip 48318538d: 18 survived, 1 killed: authenticate_user mutmut_27 `before_hash(None)`, by TestAuthenticateUserBeforeHashReceivesTheUser, RED on a git-archive tree). (1) `token_type` is deliberately ignored by `signing_algorithm` (`del token_type`), so every mutant of what is PASSED to it is unobservable: accepted_algorithms_2, verify_token_9/10/12/14 (10: `expected_type or ACCESS`->`and` only changes the value handed to those two functions; the real type check uses `expected_type` directly). (2) verify_token_1: `token_algorithm = None`->`""`: only read through `token_algorithm and ...`, both falsy. (3) authenticate_user_17/20/23: the `getattr(user, "allow_local_fallback", <default>)` default of a non-nullable mapped column is never consulted on a real User row (`bool(None)` is also False). (4) _create_password_context_9/34: dropping `default=` leaves the first scheme as default, which is the one named; _15/17/19/40/42/44: passlib resolves scheme names case-insensitively (PasslibWarning only), `ctx.schemes()` is identical. The previous 19 was last measured 2026-08-28; the code changed since (token_type plumbing, password normalisation).

column5: 175 -> 79 (measured three times before trusted: two intermediate runs raced a concurrent agent's pre-commit stash/restore against an uncommitted MODULE_TESTS edit and had to be discarded as NOT stale_cache=0). Every one of the 175 read and classified: 96 real, all killed by tests/unit/auth_dependencies/test_dependencies_survivor_mutants.py (registered in MODULE_TESTS, coverage steady at 94%) — dominated by two families: HTTPException response-body dict/headers exact-equality (existing suites checked `detail["code"]` or a truthy message, never the exact string/key/headers, so a reworded message or a renamed `"message"` key survived) and predicates/boundaries/dropped-arguments with real consequences (banner-ack tzinfo normalization + its `>=`/`>` boundary, account-expiry `<`/`<=` boundary, the JWT `algorithms=` allowlist actually reaching `jwt.decode`, the httpOnly-cookie fallback, `request.state.user_id`/`org_id` stamping, `_enforce_approval`'s `db` argument reaching `approval_required` rather than a process-cache fallback, `verify_external_token` receiving the real `request`, the TESTING-only mock user's fields, `_route_path`'s strip-charset/length boundary). 52 noise (log-only strings/branches, plus `_enforce_proxy_identity_consistency`'s `revoke_all_sessions(reason=...)` — confirmed by reading the callee that `reason` only ever reaches its own log calls). 27 equivalent, MEASURED not guessed: 3 mutants (`_banner_requirement`'s `or`->`and`, and both `accepted_algorithms(None)` siblings) were first written up as real, given tests, and reported SURVIVED on `--verify` — each then got a written equivalence proof rather than a second guess (`_banner_requirement`: `hasattr(None,"query")` is already False so the `or`'s first disjunct is a strict subset of the second, and the enclosing `try/except` closes the remaining gap; `accepted_algorithms(None)`: `core.security.signing_algorithm` discards its argument). The other 24: 18 `getattr(user/external_user, "<mapped column>", DEFAULT)` mutants where only DEFAULT changed — every caller in this module is a genuine SQLAlchemy `User` ORM instance (verified empirically: an unset mapped column returns `None`, never raises), so the default is dead code; `_route_path`'s inner default neutralised by its own outer `or ""`; 3 case-only `TESTING` env-fallback variants neutralised by `.lower()`; 2 `TokenPayload(jti=...)` mutants whose field is constructed and never read. No production bug found — every real gap was existing correct behaviour that lacked an assertion. Full reasoning: tests/unit/auth_dependencies/test_dependencies_survivor_mutants.py. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-28 from scratch (previous logs predated the completion+source-binding evidence this file's header describes, so they were NOT MEASURED under `--check-baseline` and could not be trusted): 793 mutants, 83 survived — a 4-mutant REGRESSION over this row's `79`, traced to a single intervening commit (1b536070) that added `"trigger": "fixed_date"` to `_enforce_account_expiry`'s audit `details` (making the module docstring's "AUTH_ACCOUNT_EXPIRED distinguished by details.trigger" claim true — `account_lifecycle_service.py`'s inactivity sweep already emitted `trigger="inactivity"`) with no accompanying test. All 4 (`x__enforce_account_expiry__mutmut_27/28/29/30`, the key and value each mutated two ways) confirmed REAL via `--verify`, fixed by one new test asserting the exact `details` dict (`TestEnforceAccountExpiry::test_the_audit_details_are_tagged_with_the_fixed_date_trigger`), re-verified KILLED. The other 78 survivors were confirmed byte-identical to the prior triage (git diff of the module between the two measurements touches only the 4-line `details=` literal, so every other function's mutants are unchanged; spot-checked two — `_enforce_proxy_identity_consistency`'s `mutmut_12`/`mutmut_33` — against `--show` and both match the documented getattr-DEFAULT and `revoke_all_sessions(reason=)` classes). Count returns to 79 after the fix; this row's `79`/`93` need no change. || 2026-11-12 (#1373): ceiling lowered 79 -> 30 = this file's share of the last whole-module log (cb357005f, pre-split), by function. column1: password_policy
column5: 46 -> 31 of 406 (coverage 100%, floor 94): v0.6.0 password normalisation gained tests in the mutate/password_policy lane; measured at the committed test hash, harness now finds .env.example from backend/mutants. PRIOR NOTE: 86 -> 46 of 292, and 46 is a FLOOR unless password_policy.py itself changes: every one of the 46 was classified from its diff and the classification then MEASURED. 40 killed by the new tests/unit/test_password_policy_mutants.py (registered in MODULE_TESTS, coverage 94% -> 100%), and the 46 left are EXACTLY the 43 noise + 3 equivalent predicted before the run, id for id. The 43 noise all sit in check_password_history's degradation report — the logger.warning/logger.exception strings, the 7 fragments of the operator %s message, and the checked/unverifiable counters, whose surviving `+=`->`-=` forms cannot move the level selector, traced (the critical-vs-error LEVEL split, which is what an alert keys off, is already pinned by test_password_policy_controls.py). The 3 equivalent: the wrapper's new_password_hash="" -> None/"XXXX" (the method never reads that parameter) and history_count <= 0 -> < 0 (the two disagree only at 0, where the mutant falls through to password_history[:0], an empty slice, and returns True anyway). The 40 kills were each control-verified BEFORE the run by monkeypatching the individual mutant function from the gitignored mutants/ copy and watching a test fail — with the unmutated __mutmut_orig, the 3 equivalents and 3 noise mutants as negative controls, all of which correctly reported SURVIVED (the first version of that harness reported KILLED for everything, including orig, because a stray /tmp/token.py shadowed the stdlib). Biggest real gaps closed: the module-level wrappers (get_days_until_expiration/is_password_expired/password_expiry_cutoff) were never called with an explicit current_time, so dropping the caller's clock and answering "as of now" was invisible; is_password_expired's <= cutoff boundary and its return True for a NULL password_changed_at; every tzinfo normalisation in expiry_cutoff/is_password_expired/get_days_until_expiration (3 mutants each, all killed at once by a naive input, which raises TypeError); max_age_days <= 0 -> <= 1 and history_count <= 0 -> <= 1, each turning the smallest configurable nonzero value into a second off switch; and the uppercase/lowercase/digit error strings, which are response-body text the SPA renders, not log output. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-28 from scratch (source unchanged since 73775294, the wave-2 commit that added min_age_hours BEFORE this baseline was first set — checked via `git log`, so the 292-mutant count already covers it): a clean `--clean` + `--module password_policy` run against a real `.meta`-backed log reproduced 292 mutants / 46 survived / 100% coverage exactly, and `--check-baseline password_policy` reports "holding at 46" (not NOT MEASURED — this module now has real completion evidence, unlike the 2026-08-12-era logs the header above warns about). All 46 survivors were individually run through `--verify`: 45/46 CONFIRMED-SURVIVED (0 KILLED, i.e. no stale/wrong mutmut verdicts), 1 UNVERIFIABLE (the `history_count <= 0 -> < 0` equivalent, mutmut's diff-apply matched 0 context lines against the docstring-adjacent line — confirmed equivalent instead by direct control-flow trace: at history_count==0 the mutant falls through to `password_history[:0]`, an empty slice, so `unverifiable` stays 0 and the function still returns True). Every one of the 46 diffs was also read by hand against the classification above and found to match: no diff touches a return value, an exception path, or the `logger.critical if checked == 0 else logger.error` LEVEL selector — every one is confined to the degradation-report's %s/%d message content or a counter that only feeds it. No new real findings; no fix needed. RE-MEASURED 2026-09-12 (git_commit=07390a49): only the ratchet's `.meta` fingerprint had gone stale, not the count. Issue #810's auth-state isolation work edited tests/unit/test_auth_config_behaviour.py (registered in MODULE_TESTS[password_policy]) to add a missing `monkeypatch.setattr(lockout, "_last_redis_probe", 0.0)` reset and to opt into the new shared tests/fixtures/auth_state_isolation.py plugin — app/auth/password_policy.py itself was NOT touched (unchanged since 73775294). Ran in an isolated per-lane worktree (.claude/worktrees/mut-pwpolicy) against a throwaway Postgres on 127.0.0.1:55435 (never the live dev stack): a clean `--clean` + `--module password_policy` reproduced 292 mutants / 46 survived / 100% coverage exactly, and `--check-baseline password_policy` reports "holding at 46" (exit 0). No new survivors, no reclassification needed — the 46 are the same set this row already documents.
